title: Gum inflammation and periodontitis: protecting tooth support
intro: Gingivitis is inflammation of the gums, commonly caused by plaque. Periodontitis affects deeper tooth-supporting tissues and bone. It can progress with little pain, so the absence of toothache does not mean gums are healthy.

sections.heading: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: Bleeding during brushing, redness, persistent bad breath, gum recession or loose teeth deserve attention. Smoking can mask bleeding while increasing risk; diabetes and some medicines also influence gum health.

sections.heading: Assessment and tests
paragraphs: A dental professional checks plaque, pocket depth, bleeding and tooth stability; selected X-rays assess bone loss. Explain smoking, diabetes, medicines and difficulty cleaning specific areas. Bring your medicine list and previous results; ask which findings would change the plan.

sections.heading: Treatment choices
paragraphs: Professional removal of deposits above and below the gumline, home cleaning and maintenance are central. Some cases need surgery; antibiotics are not routine substitutes for cleaning or an individualized dental plan. Agree how benefit and adverse effects will be checked before changing treatment.

sections.heading: Everyday care
paragraphs: Brush gently with fluoride toothpaste and clean between teeth using tools matched to the gaps. Ask for a demonstration. Do not stop cleaning solely because inflamed gums bleed, and seek smoking-cessation support. Choose a routine you can maintain, and discuss barriers such as cost, work or language.

sections.heading: Follow-up and warning signs
paragraphs: Arrange dental review for persistent bleeding or loose teeth. Facial swelling, fever or worsening pain need urgent dental advice; difficulty swallowing or breathing with swelling requires emergency care.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira avoids brushing a bleeding area. A dental demonstration helps her clean gently while receiving treatment for the underlying inflammation.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben’s teeth feel stable after treatment. He still attends maintenance visits because comfort alone cannot show whether gum pockets remain controlled.
